subject.title: fix(gateway): enforce plugin-ownership check in sessions.patch

question: Should plugin-runtime `sessions.patch` fail closed for every legacy ownerless session row, or must OpenClaw provide an explicit ownership migration/adoption path before enforcing that rule?
rationale: Strict equality closes the cross-plugin authority ambiguity, but it also removes an existing capability for persisted pre-ownership rows; tests establish mechanics, not the intended upgrade and authorization policy.

options.title: Approve fail-closed
options.body: Reject all ownerless rows for plugin runtimes and document/prove that operators or non-plugin clients remain the recovery path.

options.title: Add ownership migration
options.body: Provide a doctor or explicit operator flow that safely assigns ownership before strict plugin-runtime enforcement.

options.title: Preserve ownerless access
options.body: Continue allowing plugin runtimes to patch ownerless rows, accepting ambiguous authority and potential adoption by the first caller.

recommendation.title: Approve fail-closed
recommendation.body: Reject all ownerless rows for plugin runtimes and document/prove that operators or non-plugin clients remain the recovery path.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced the current plugin-runtime/session ownership contract and existing delete fence, so they have the strongest history signal for the intended ownerless-row policy.
